-104.title: What is the Safe, how do I open it, and how do I take items out?
-104.html:
The Safe is a special storage container that holds items you receive from the Battle Pass and lobby events.

How it works:

  • If a reward is a physical item (not a skin), it's placed in your Safe on the server.

  • The Safe is take-out only — you can move items out of it, but you can't put anything into it.

  • After a server wipe, the Safe is locked for a certain period to maintain game balance, so your rewards aren't available right at the start of a new wipe.

  • On Premium servers the Safe is not available at all — it's switched off there permanently, so rewards can't be collected on a Premium server. Nothing is lost: everything stays in the Safe and can be collected on any other server type

How to open it and take items out:

  1. Join a server where you want to unpack your rewards (any server type except Premium).

  2. Open your Inventory, then open the Safe.

  3. Select an item in the Safe and move it into your inventory.

  4. The item is now in your inventory — use or equip it as usual.

-115.title: Why can't I repair or upgrade my walls while my base is being raided?
-115.html:
When your base takes damage from siege weapons used by players not authorized on your Tool Cupboard, a temporary effect called Raid Defense activates.

  • While effect is active, you cannot upgrade building pieces (wood to stone to metal) or repair them with a mallet.
  • This applies only to the specific element that was hit - other parts of your base remain fully repairable.
  • The block lasts for a set time after the last hit.
  • Once the timer runs out, you can repair and upgrade normally again.
  • Your own teammates cannot accidentally trigger this - it only activates from damage by unauthorized players.

-112.title: What are ziplines and power line towers, and how do I use them to travel?
-112.html:
Ziplines and power line towers:

  • Tall metal power line towers are placed across the map, connected by wires that stretch over forests, fields, and hills.
  • You can use these wires as ziplines to travel quickly between towers at height.
  • While riding a zipline, you fly over the landscape, which gives you both a speed advantage and a bird's-eye view of the area below.
  • The towers themselves have platforms with loot crates and barrels, making them worth visiting even if you don't need to travel.
  • Be careful though - you are exposed and easy to spot from the ground while on a zipline or standing on a tower.

-113.title: What are metal window bars and how do they help defend my base?
-113.html:
Metal window bars are a defensive building element that you can install in window frames.

  • They cover the opening with heavy metal plates, leaving a narrow slot for shooting.
  • This protects most of your body from incoming bullets while still allowing you to fire back.
  • They are especially useful during raids and base defense.

-108.title: What are Weapon Attachments?
-108.html:
• When you craft a firearm, it is randomly assigned attachment slots - the number of slots depends on the weapon type and can range from zero to three.

  • These slots allow you to equip attachments such as sights (Holosight, Optical Scope) and other modifications that improve weapon performance.

  • The number of slots you receive is determined at the moment of crafting and cannot be changed afterward, so crafting the same weapon multiple times may yield different slot configurations.

-118.title: Where do I find traders and what do they sell?
-118.html:
• Traders are NPCs located at points of interest across the map.
  • Each trader specializes in a specific category of goods - for example, one sells weapons, attachments, and ammo, while another offers resources or tools.
  • You trade with them using in-game resources.
  • Traders are part of the game's economy and offer a way to get valuable gear without crafting it yourself.

-131.title: How do I toggle teammate visibility on the map?
-131.html:
Use the control buttons on the left side of the map screen.

When the "Teammates" icon is green, they are visible. When it is grey, they are hidden.

-122.title: How does the code lock work and what happens if I enter the wrong code?
-122.html:
You can place a code lock on doors and storage to protect them with a numeric password.

  • The system penalizes failed attempts - each wrong code you enter has consequences, so you cannot simply try every combination until you get lucky.
  • Set a code you can remember, and share it only with trusted teammates.

-124.title: Why is the mallet missing from crafting and why does it appear automatically?
-124.html:
• The mallet is no longer a craftable item - that is why you cannot find it in the crafting menu.
  • It is now built into the building system and appears automatically in your character's hands when you tap the Build button in the HUD.
  • You do not need to craft, find, or carry it in your inventory.
  • The mallet is used for placing new structures, upgrading them to higher tiers, repairing damaged pieces, and demolishing recently placed objects.
  • Mallet skins are temporarily unavailable but will be restored soon - you will be able to choose which previously purchased skin to use by default.

-177.title: How to find and join a Clan?
-177.html:
You can find and join Clans in Oxide: Survival Island through the Clan List or by accepting an invite.

Finding Clans via the Clan List

  1. Open the Clan menu and tap Clan List.

  2. Browse available clans. You can filter by:

  • All - no filter

  • Unlimited - clans with auto-join enabled

  • Application Required - players must apply to join the clan

  • Tap on a clan to view its details.

  • Tap Join to apply or join instantly (depending on the clan's join method).

Quick Start

Use the Quick Start button to instantly join a random clan that has auto-join enabled.

Joining via Invite

Another player can invite you to their clan. You'll receive the invite and can accept or decline it.

Important Notes

  • If a clan uses Manual join, the Leader or Officers must approve your application. Applications expire after 7 days.

  • After joining a clan, you must wait 2 hours before joining another.

  • You can apply to a clan even if it's currently full - your application will be queued.

-176.title: How to create a Clan?
-176.html:
To create a Clan in Oxide: Survival Island, your account must be at least Level 5. Once you reach Level 5, follow these steps:

  1. Open the Clan menu from the main screen.

  2. Tap Create Clan.

  3. Enter your Clan Name (4-12 characters, must be unique).

  4. Enter your Clan Tag (2-6 characters).

  5. Select your Language.

  6. Optionally fill in the About section (up to 100 characters) and Announcement (up to 100 characters).

  7. Choose a Join Method
    - Application required (players must apply to join the clan)
    - Unlimited (any player can join the clan without approval)
    - By invitation only (you can join a clan via an invitation from the leader)

  8. Set the Required Level for new members

Once created, you become the Leader of the clan with full management permissions.

-180.title: Clan ranks and permissions
-180.html:
Every Clan in Oxide: Survival Island has three ranks with different permission levels.

Leader

Each Clan has exactly one Leader - the player who created the Clan. The Leader has full control:

  • Invite and kick any member (including Officers)

  • Change the Clan avatar, name, tag, description, and announcement

  • Assign or remove Officers (up to 3)

  • Change Clan settings (join method, required level)

  • Transfer leadership to another member

The Leader must transfer leadership before they can leave the Clan.

Officer

A Clan can have up to 3 Officers, appointed by the Leader. Officers can:

  • Invite new players to the Clan

  • Kick regular members (but not other Officers or the Leader)

  • Approve or decline join applications (if manual join is enabled)

Officers cannot change Clan settings, assign other Officers, or kick Officers.

Member

Regular members can:

  • View Clan information and member list

  • Leave the clan at any time, starting 2 hours after joining

Regular members cannot invite, kick, or manage Clan settings.

-178.title: How to invite or kick players in your Clan?
-178.html:
As a Leader or Officer in a Clan, you can invite new members and remove existing ones

Inviting Players

How to invite players to your clan:

  1. Open the Clans menu.

  2. Tap on Participants.

  3. Use the Player Search to find and invite specific users.

Kicking Players

  • The Leader can kick any member, including Officers.

  • Officers can kick regular members, but cannot kick other Officers or the Leader.

To kick a player, open the Clan member list, tap on the player, and select Kick.

Who Can Invite and Kick?

  • Leader: Can invite and kick anyone.

  • Officers: Can invite anyone and kick regular members only.

  • Regular members: Cannot invite or kick players.

-193.title: What is the Chainsaw and how does it work?
-193.html:
Q1. What fuel does it use and how long does a full tank last?

The Chainsaw uses Low Grade Fuel. A full tank holds 50 cans = 25 minutes of non-stop operation. You refuel and unload it the same way as firearms - press Reload to top up to 50 cans (or whatever you have), and use the unload action to take fuel back out.

Q2. Does the Chainsaw lose durability when I just hold the trigger?

No - but it still burns fuel. Fuel drains the whole time the action button is held, including idle. Durability is only spent when the saw is actually cutting a valid target (tree, wooden structure, or flesh). Holding the trigger in the air wastes fuel but not durability.

Q3. What can I cut, and what doesn't work?

Valid targets: trees, animal/player corpses, and any wooden buildings (walls, doors, fences). Invalid targets: stone, metal, and HQM structures - the saw will spark on them but deal no damage.

Q4. Why don't I have to aim at the red X marks on trees?

Every valid hit on a tree automatically counts as a marker hit (auto-crit). You just hold the action button on the trunk - no micro-aiming required. This makes wood farming faster and more consistent than with the axe.

Q5. How much durability does it have, how do I repair it, and what happens at 0?

Max durability is 100. Repair cost: 10 HQM, 20 Metal Fragments, 1 Metal Sheet. At 0 durability the engine stalls and the saw stops working - but you can still unload remaining fuel from the tank.

-182.title: What's the difference between a Clan and a Team?
-182.html:
Oxide: Survival Island has two separate social systems: Clans and Teams. They serve different purposes and work independently of each other.

Clans. This is just the beginning - more clan features are in development. Stay tuned!

Clans

A Clan is a larger social group up to 15 for community and communication. Clan features include:

  • Clans have a rank system (Leader, Officer, Member).

  • Clans appear in the Clan List where other players can find and join them.

Teams

A Team is a small group of up to 5 players who play together on a server. Team features include:

  • Team members have their own markers and colors visible on the map.

  • You can see teammate HP bars and names highlighted.

  • Teams persist across servers - your team stays the same no matter which server you join.

  • Teams have a dedicated Group voice channel.

Key Differences

  • Size: Teams are small (up to 5), Clans are larger (up to 15)

  • Purpose: Teams are for direct gameplay cooperation, Clans are for community and social features.

  • You can be in both a Team and a Clan at the same time.

-189.title: Why did my base split into several separate buildings?
-189.html:
If your base suddenly became two or more separate structures, here's why.

Your base is treated as a single building only when all parts are fully connected. Connection means side-to-side contact between structural blocks - for example, a foundation flush against another foundation. Small touches, corners, or overlaps do NOT count as a connection.

If a structural element is removed or destroyed and the remaining pieces are no longer fully connected, the system automatically splits the structure into separate buildings.

What changes after a split:

  • The Tool Cupboard (TC) stays in only one of the resulting buildings

  • The other parts no longer have a TC - they begin to decay

  • You can place a new TC on those parts (subject to building privilege rules)

  • Items inside (chests, workbenches, etc.) try to power from the TC of whichever part they're in

→ See also: Why can't I place a Tool Cupboard? · How do I merge two buildings into one?

-188.title: Why can't I place a Repair Cupboard?
-188.html:
Trouble placing a Repair Cupboard (Tool Cupboard)? Here are the main reasons and how to fix them.

A cupboard can only be placed if all of these are true:

  • No other protected building is too close. A cupboard can't be placed near the structural elements of a building that already has one — this is the most common reason

  • You have building privilege on the spot: either no other cupboard controls this area, or you're authorized by it

  • The structural element you're standing on belongs to a building that doesn't already have a cupboard — one per building

  • The spot isn't blocked by terrain or other structures

How to tell which one it is. If you see "Cupboard privilege required to build here", you're inside someone else's cupboard zone. If you see "Can't stack building privileges", this building already has a cupboard, or another protected building is too close — move further away from it and try again.

If none of the above applies and you still can't place it, please submit a Bug Report.

→ See also: Why did my base split into multiple buildings? · How do building privileges work?

-208.title: What is the Military Armor, where do I find it, and does it protect from radiation?

-224.title: What is the railroad for? How do I drive the train?
-224.html:
Railroad tracks run across the island, including through the winter biome — they're a handy landmark for navigation, and you can walk and drive along them. And a working train now runs on them.

Trains have no owner: anyone can board one, and whoever reaches the controls first drives.

Driving it
Walk up to the lever in the locomotive cab and take the controls. You have three forward gears, three reverse gears and neutral, plus a horn. Stay next to the lever — step away and you let go of the controls.
To change direction at a junction, hold left or right as you approach. If there's a branch on that side, the train takes it; otherwise it carries straight on.

Fuel
The train runs on Low Grade Fuel, poured into the tank on the body. Trains spawn with fuel already in them, and a gauge shows how much is left. Out of fuel the lever still moves but the train won't pull — top it up and it goes again. The higher the gear, the faster you go and the faster the fuel burns.

Cargo
Both the locomotive and the wagon have a cargo hold with loot in it. The holds aren't locked — anyone who walks up can open them, so don't use a train as storage.

Riding it
You can stand, walk, jump and aim on the deck while the train is moving. The train never hurts the people it's carrying.

Being hit by one
Standing on the track is a bad idea: a moving train knocks players, animals and vehicles aside and damages them. The faster it's going, the more it hurts. At walking pace it's harmless.

Where trains come from, and how they disappear
Trains appear on their own on free sidings around the map — there's no schedule. A train left where it spawned stays put, but once it's been moved it starts to wear down and will eventually break apart, so a train you park somewhere won't be waiting the next day. A rake of wagons with no working locomotive also breaks down.

Can it be destroyed?
Yes, at any time — trains aren't protected by the no-raid window. You can repair one with a hammer for metal fragments. A destroyed train leaves a wreck and drops whatever was in its cargo.

You also can't build on or near the tracks: there's a permanent no-build corridor along the whole railway.

-241.title: What is the backpack and how do I get one?
-241.html:
The backpack is a wearable item that adds a separate storage section of 10 slots to your inventory. It goes into its own fifth equipment slot, and its contents live behind a tab on the inventory screen.

How to get one. Research it at the workbench, then craft it.

What you can't put in it. Personal items can't be placed in the backpack section.

Resources are spent from it automatically. When something costs materials, the game takes them from the backpack too — you don't have to move anything out by hand before crafting.

When your character dies, the backpack and everything inside it drop as a single container that anyone can loot. When you log out, the section stays with the sleeping body and can be looted there behind a second tab, just like the rest of the inventory.

-232.title: A train disappeared or was destroyed — what happens to it and to the loot inside?
-232.html:
First things first: trains don't belong to anyone. There's no owner, no lock and no claim on a train — any player can walk up to the one you're using, take the controls and drive off with it.

Why a train disappears

  • Someone drove it away. The most common reason.

  • It wore down. A train starts to wear down as soon as it's been moved from where it appeared, and will eventually break apart on its own. A train still standing on the exact siding where it appeared doesn't wear down at all. A rake of wagons with no working locomotive also breaks down.

  • It was destroyed by players. Trains have no protection and the no-raid window doesn't cover them, so anyone can shoot one at any time.

What happens when a train is destroyed

  • It leaves a wreck on the track, and everything from its cargo holds drops on the spot — which means whoever destroyed it can simply pick the loot up.

  • The destruction itself is dangerous. A destroyed train explodes, so standing right next to one that's about to break is a bad idea. Move away.

Repairing one

A train can be repaired with a hammer for metal fragments. That restores its health and holds off the wear, so a train you're actively using can be kept going — but it can't be made permanent.

What this means for your loot

Never use a train as storage. The cargo holds aren't locked, so anyone who walks up can empty them — and if the train is destroyed or wears out, everything inside ends up on the ground for anyone to take. You also can't protect a train with a Tool Cupboard or build anything on it.

Anything you put in a train should be treated as temporary. Because trains don't belong to players, lost trains and their cargo aren't restored.

-242.title: I took off my backpack and my items fell out. Why?
-242.html:
The storage section belongs to the backpack itself, so when you take the backpack off, its contents have nowhere to stay — they drop on the ground at your feet as a single bag. This happens even if your inventory has free space.

Pick the bag up right away. Anyone can loot it while it's lying there, and it disappears once it's empty. You can only take items out of it, not put them back in.

-32.title: How do Sleeping Bags and Beds (respawn points) work, how many can I place, and can I rename them?
-32.html:
You can now give each Sleeping Bag or Bed its own custom name - easy to tell respawn points apart across bases and react instantly during raids

Sleeping Bags and Beds are your personal respawn points. Place them wherever you need - and respawn at one of them.

  • You can have up to 10 respawn points. Placing an 11th automatically removes your oldest.

  • After you respawn at a point, it goes on a cooldown, points placed close together share that cooldown, so stacking many in one spot won't let you respawn instantly.

  • You can only respawn if the spot is clear - if it's blocked, you respawn normally instead.

  • You can give each Sleeping Bag or Bed its own custom name, so it's easy to tell your respawn points apart and react instantly during raids.

  • Respawn points belong to you.

-43.title: What is Health and how do I manage it?
-43.html:
Health represents your character's survival status.

  • Your health is reduced by damage from other players, animals, hunger, thirst, radiation, cold, and falling.
  • Health regenerates slowly when you avoid combat and maintain adequate hunger and thirst levels.
  • Wearing better armor reduces incoming damage.
  • Use bandages and medkits to restore health quickly.

-44.title: How do I manage Hunger?
-44.html:
Hunger decreases over time and will eventually damage your health if left unchecked.

  • Sources of Food: Restore hunger by eating gathered or hunted items such as fish, meat, and other provisions.
  • Cooking: Cooking food before eating makes it more nutritious - for example, cooked meat is much better than raw meat.
  • How to Eat: You can eat or drink by tapping "Consume" in your inventory or by placing items in quick slots and pressing the action button.

Important Mechanics:

  • Offline Consumption: Much like thirst, your hunger bar continues to drop in real-time, even when you are offline or inside your base.
  • Survival Risk: Your character remains active in the world while you are away. If the hunger bar reaches zero, your character will lose health and may die before you log back in.

-29.title: What are sleepers and what happens to my character when I log out?
-29.html:
• When you log out of the game, your character does not disappear - it stays in the world as a "sleeper."
  • Your sleeper remains at the exact location where you logged out, lying on the ground with all your inventory and equipment still on them.
  • Other players can find your sleeper, kill it, and take everything.
  • Your sleeper also continues to consume food and water while you are offline - if either reaches zero, the character dies and drops all loot.
  • To protect yourself, always log out inside your base behind locked doors.
  • Also, never log out while standing in water - your character will drown and die. To protect yourself, always log out inside your base behind locked doors and on dry ground.

-45.title: How do I manage Thirst?
-45.html:
Ways to stay hydrated:

  • Water Bottles: Loot them from boxes found across the map.
  • Ice Shards: Gather these exclusively in the Frost Biome.
  • Food: Consuming certain food items will also replenish your thirst bar.

Key Survival Mechanics:

  • Desert Biome: Heat causes thirst to deplete significantly faster.
  • Health Loss: If your thirst bar hits zero, you will begin losing HP.
  • Real-Time Consumption: Thirst depletes constantly, even while you are offline or inside your base. Your character remains active in the world at all times.

💡 Pro Tip: Always top up your hydration and keep spare water in your inventory before logging out to ensure your character survives until you return.

-46.title: How do I eat and drink items?
-46.html:
You can use food, water, and other consumables in two ways:

  • From Inventory: Open your inventory, select the item, and tap the "Consume" button.
  • Via Quick Slots: Place items into your Quick Slots for faster access. During gameplay, simply tap the corresponding action button to use the item immediately without opening your menu.

-65.title: What biomes exist in the game and how do they differ?
-65.html:
• Winter - A snow-covered biome where cold weather drains your health, and the effect intensifies the deeper you venture into it. Nights are especially dangerous. However, this biome has higher ore density and is the only place to find Ice Shards. Player density tends to be lower here. To survive, wear Leather Armor for warmth, place Campfires and Furnaces near your base, and avoid prolonged exposure without protection.
  • Desert - A sandy biome with scarce vegetation. The heat causes hunger and thirst to deplete faster than in other areas. Always carry plenty of food and water supplies when exploring the desert.
  • Forest - A green, balanced biome with the most trees and a wide variety of resources. It's the most popular area for building bases, but the high player and animal density makes it more dangerous and competitive.
  • Water - Water areas significantly slow your movement but are the primary source of fish.

-52.title: What are Skins?
-52.html: Skins (for weapons, armor, and other items) are cosmetic overlays, not actual weapons or items. A skin does not give you the item itself. You must first unlock the corresponding item's blueprint at a Workbench on the server. Once the item is unlocked, you can select the purchased skin during crafting and craft the item with that skin applied.

-69.title: What types of loot containers exist?
-69.html:
• Barrels: The main source of scrap and components. Found in and near cars and scattered across the map.
  • Wooden Crate: Contains random loot including resources, Water Bottles, Tarp, Anti-Radiation Pills, axes, armor, and components. Found in cities, gas stations, and radiation zones.
  • Military Box: Found in radiation zones and military vehicles on roads. Contains more scrap than regular loot boxes.
  • Tool Box: Found in cars along roads. Red colored and contains tool-related resources.

-72.title: What is the Repair Cupboard?
-72.html:
The Repair Cupboard (Tool Cupboard) controls building rights and your base territory.

  • Whoever accesses it controls your base, so always lock it.

  • It now has 24 slots for storing upkeep resources - keeping it stocked prevents your structures from decaying.

  • Only one can be placed per building, on a foundation.

  • Anyone who opens your cupboard is authorized on it automatically — there's no button to press and no confirmation. This is why locking the cupboard matters: an unlocked one hands building rights to the first player who reaches it.

  • Only the player who placed the cupboard can take authorization away. Standing at it, they can either remove a single player from the authorized list, or use CLEAR to wipe the whole list at once. They can't remove themselves, and this right can't be passed to anyone else.

  • Monitor its durability, as it can be damaged.

  • Its build-zone covers the structural elements of the building it's in. See "How do building privileges and build zones work?"

-70.title: What vehicles are available?
-70.html:
What ground vehicles are available?

Buggy: A light, fast off-road single-seat vehicle. Excellent for scouting and quick raids. The open design leaves the driver vulnerable to attacks. The Buggy is an Item with Mechanics - purchasing it in the Main Shop only unlocks the crafting blueprint. To get the actual vehicle, connect to a server, open your Craft Menu, gather all the required components, and craft it. Spawn it on a permitted area via quick slots. Control it with gas, brake, and steering buttons. Only one vehicle can be spawned at a time. The buggy can run over enemies.

What air vehicles are available?

Helicopter (Copter): A compact single-seat helicopter for quick travel avoiding ground obstacles. Like the Buggy, the Copter is an Item with Mechanics - purchasing it in the Main Shop only unlocks the crafting blueprint in your Craft Menu (Other section). You still need to gather all required components on the server and craft it before you can use it. Controls include Gas for ascending, Left/Right for body rotation, Joystick for forward tilt, and an Exit button. Only one can be spawned at a time. It's vulnerable to attacks but offers tactical advantages through height and speed. Requires piloting skill to operate effectively.

Static Transport: Ziplines & Power Lines

Power Line Towers: Tall metal towers are placed across the map, connected by wires stretching over forests and hills.

  • Travel: You can use these wires as ziplines to travel quickly between towers at height.
  • Loot: Towers have platforms with loot crates and barrels.
  • Risk: You are exposed and easy to spot from the ground while on a zipline.

-75.title: What is the Workbench? How do I unlock weapons, armor, and craft ammo?
-75.html:
The Workbench unlocks advanced item crafting.

  • Research: Blueprints require a specific amount of Scrap to research.
  • Persistence: Once researched, the recipe is added to your crafting menu on that specific server and remains unlocked until the next server wipe.
  • Necessity: It is essential for crafting all high-tier items and equipment.

-73.html:
• Small Storage Box: Stores items and resources but cannot be locked. Offers weak protection and should be monitored for durability.
  • Large Storage Box: More storage slots than small boxes. Can be locked with Key Locks or Code Locks. Offers better protection.

• Safe Zones are areas where player-versus-player (PvP) damage is disabled.
  • These zones exist around the Lucky Wheel, the Forester, and the Miner.
  • The HUD displays an indicator showing when you're inside a safe zone.

-74.title: What cooking appliances are there?
-74.html:
• Furnace: Smelts ores into materials and can also be used for cooking food - you can roast meat and mushrooms in it just like on a campfire. Add wood as fuel and place smeltable resources (Iron Ore, Sulfur Ore, HQ Metal Ore) or food in the upper slot. Burning wood produces charcoal as a byproduct. Emits light and smoke.
  • Campfire: Provides light, warmth, and can cook food. Place indoors or outdoors. Add wood as fuel and place food in the upper slot to cook. Emits visible light and smoke-use cautiously at night.
  • Cauldron: Cooks food like a campfire. Functions the same way-add fuel and place food.

citadel-221.title: What is the Military Base (Citadel), how do I get inside, and how does the radar work?
citadel-221.html:
The Military Base — shown on the map as Citadel — is the most dangerous location on the island, and the loot matches the risk.

  • It's patrolled by armed guards. You can tell their rank by armour colour: green — the easiest, blue — tougher, red — the hardest. Don't come with a bow or spear: bring good weapons, plenty of meds and ideally a team.

  • An anti-air turret on the base shoots at helicopters.

  • Killing a guard has a chance to drop a Military Base Keycard. It can't be crafted.

  • Take the keycard to the radar in the centre, climb to the roof from the outside and insert it into the Access Terminal. The keycard is consumed.

  • The dish activates and calls airdrops onto the base — everyone nearby is notified, so expect company.

  • After that the radar goes on cooldown — if you try to activate it during that time, you'll see a "system recharging" message.

  • It's patrolled by armed guards. You can tell their rank by armour colour: green — the easiest, blue — tougher, red — the hardest. They walk fixed routes, stop at points to watch the area, use cover, throw smoke grenades and return to patrolling once a fight is over. They keep scanning the area even while standing still, so they'll spot you before you're in their line of sight. Don't come with a bow or spear: bring good weapons, plenty of meds and ideally a team.

quick-craft-47.title: What is the Craft Menu? What is Quick Craft / the new crafting menu? Why does the craft menu look different now?
quick-craft-47.html:
The Craft Menu is the main interface for creating items in the game. You can access it by tapping the crafting button inside your inventory screen.

The menu is divided into the following categories for easy navigation: All Items, Tools, Ammunition, Weapons, Clothing, Components, and Other.

Some recipes are available from the start, while others are locked. To unlock a locked recipe, you need to collect Scrap and spend it at a Workbench to learn the blueprint. Once learned, the recipe becomes available in your Craft Menu.

The crafting menu has been redesigned and now has a Quick Craft tab that automatically scans your inventory and shows everything you can craft right now with the materials you're carrying - craft what you need (bandages, ammo) in one tap.
